column2: slub: protect put_cpu_partial() with disabled irqs instead of cmpxchg

column1: Jann Horn reported [1] the following theoretically possible race:
task A: put_cpu_partial() calls preempt_disable()
task A: oldpage = this_cpu_read(s->cpu_slab->partial)
interrupt: kfree() reaches unfreeze_partials() and discards the page
task B (on another CPU): reallocates page as page cache
task A: reads page->pages and page->pobjects
halves of the pointer page->lru.prev
task B (on another CPU): frees page
interrupt: allocates page as SLUB page and places it on the percpu partial list
task A: this_cpu_cmpxchg() succeeds
which would cause page->pages and page->pobjects to end up containing
halves of pointers that would then influence when put_cpu_partial()
happens and show up in root-only sysfs files. Maybe that's acceptable
I don't know. But there should probably at least be a comment for now
to point out that we're reading union fields of a page that might be
in a completely different state.
Additionally
column2: the this_cpu_cmpxchg() approach in put_cpu_partial() is only safe

column1: against s->cpu_slab->partial manipulation in ___slab_alloc() if the latter
disables irqs
column2: otherwise a __slab_free() in an irq handler could call

column1: put_cpu_partial() in the middle of ___slab_alloc() manipulating ->partial
and corrupt it. This becomes an issue on RT after a local_lock is introduced
in later patch. The fix means taking the local_lock also in put_cpu_partial()
on RT.
After debugging this issue
column2: Mike Galbraith suggested [2] that to avoid

column1: different locking schemes on RT and !RT
with disabled irqs (to be converted to local_lock_irqsave() later) everywhere.
This should be acceptable as it's not a fast path
partial unfreezing outside of the irq disabled section makes it short
the retry loop gone the code can be also simplified. In addition
reported by Jann should no longer be possible.
